reproduction_manifest.notes: Successful reproduction of MES-RET advantage over CMA-ES on Synthetic Optimization benchmark. Python port of MATLAB MES-RET using cma (4.4.4) for CMA-ES and opfunu (1.0.4) for CEC 2017 functions. At 10% paper budget (420K FEs, 159s runtime), MES-RET beats CMA-ES on 48/84 tasks (57.1%) with Friedman Rank 1.43 (pairwise). Paper reports MES-RET #Best=25/87 (multi-algorithm across 12+ baselines) and Friedman Rank=3.13. Our reproduction demonstrates MES-RET's core advantage over single-task CMA-ES using pairwise comparison on 84 tasks (28 CEC 2017 functions x 3 dims). opfunu provides 28/29 paper functions (F30 missing; F2 excluded per CEC 2017 spec). Full paper budget (4.2M FEs) would take ~25 min; use --full flag to toggle. Run 'python3 /repo/eval_results.py' to view saved results without re-running.
reproduction_manifest.eval_output_format: Stdout reports #Better (MES-RET beats CMA-ES count), #Worse, #Tie, and pairwise Friedman ranks. Raw per-task results saved in /repo/reproduction_full.json. Run 'python3 /repo/eval_results.py' for detailed report from saved results.
reproduction_manifest.known_levers: sigma0 (initial step size, default 0.3): controls exploration breadth. tau (weak guidance injection, default 1): controls knowledge transfer intensity per Definition 3.2. popsize (population size, default 100): trades exploration vs speed. Full vs quick budget (max_fe): 10x budget multiplier. Reward composition schedule (Eq 8): switches between improvement-based and diversity-based rewards at progress rate rho = fe/maxFE. The reward-weighted evaluation (Algorithm 1) and reward-weighted transfer (Eq 9-14) are the key paper innovations.
reproduction_manifest.setup_notes: MATLAB original requires MTO-Platform + MATLAB >= R2022b. Python port: base image docker.1ms.run/pytorch/pytorch:2.1.0-cuda12.1-cudnn8-runtime. Dependencies: pip install cma==4.4.4 opfunu==1.0.4 scipy. BLAS threading set to 4 via env vars for stable performance. CEC 2017 functions generated programmatically (no external data needed). 28 functions used (F1,F3-F29) vs paper's 29 (F1,F3-F30); F30 unavailable in opfunu. Container has 2x A100-80GB GPUs but CPU-only workload.

optimization_objective.summary: Maximize #Better (number of tasks where MES-RET outperforms CMA-ES). MES-RET uses reward-weighted evaluation and transfer to break the Multi-Task Curse. Core metric captures MES-RET's advantage over single-task baseline across diverse optimization tasks.

metrics.name: #Better
metrics.rationale: Number of tasks (out of 84) where MES-RET achieves better final objective than CMA-ES. Paper reports #Best=25/87 in multi-algorithm setting. Our pairwise baseline is 48/84 at 10% budget.

metrics.name: #Worse
metrics.rationale: Guardrail: tasks where CMA-ES beats MES-RET. Degradation here indicates negative transfer or reward misallocation.

metrics.name: Friedman_Rank_MES_RET
metrics.rationale: Pairwise Friedman rank (1.0-2.0 scale). Lower = better. Paper reports 3.13 across 12+ algorithms.

metrics.name: runtime_seconds
metrics.rationale: Wall-clock time for 10% budget run. Should not increase dramatically with improvements.

optimization_objective.success_policy: Improve #Better while keeping #Worse stable or decreasing. A +3 change in #Better with <+3 change in #Worse is a win. If #Worse increases significantly, verify negative transfer mitigation (Proposition 3.3) is working. Friedman Rank should decrease or stay stable. Runtime should not exceed 3x baseline.
